items.title: Darnell Howard Interview, 1957-04-21
items.q: You've heard of Cliff King... And Buster Bailey... I played on three of them... When Buster left Fletcher Henderson... I get the first book... That's what he had me on.

ctx.x: Was there much... Are you living in Charlie Elgar's bands?

Oh, yeah. Well, they had arrangements, you know, and things like that. And the guy took a solo. He just took a solo. You know who was in that band? You've heard of Cliff King, the Clannett player, haven't you? Yeah. And Buster Bailey. Yeah. They had another fellow from New Orleans named Lane. I don't remember his first name. His name was Lane. Uh-huh. He's a cigar maker, and he played Clannett in the band, too. But when Charlie's band busted up, he didn't play anymore.
How many pieces in Charlie Elgar's band?

items.title: Darnell Howard Interview, 1957-04-21
items.q: I got Buster Clippet King, and my fibbers come up there to hear him play the saxophone

ctx.x: Well, I had a... This particular night, I went up to the deluxe where Sidney Baixier was playing, and he's got one of these B-flat curved modern saxophone sopranos. Yes. Playing the hell out of him, no kidding. And I went back raving that next night on the job, so I got Buster Clippet King, and my fibbers come up there to hear him play the saxophone, and he don't pick it up to him. So I went up to the stand and said, Sidney, where's your saxophone? He said, it's in pawn. I said, oh, man. I said, look, you guys up…
He said, that's all right. Yeah, that's no kidding.
